public_rationale: Niantic deployed Llama 2 in Peridot in November 2023. The documented application and subsequent positive reception satisfy the modest prediction that free competing models would suit some customers. This does not establish widespread displacement of OpenAI.
limitations: Free refers to model access; deployment can still incur operating costs.
The deployment account is a supplier case study containing customer testimony, not an independent evaluation.
A strict requirement for an OpenAI-to-Llama migration would remain unproven.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Free open-source competitors to OpenAI, though perhaps not yet as good, will suit some customers.

statement.excerpt: The competitors may not (yet) be as good, but they are free, which will suit some customers fine.
statement.document_title: Top 5 reasons OpenAI is probably not worth 90 billion dollars

from_speaker: The competitors may not (yet) be as good
our_interpretation: In the surrounding discussion of openly released models, free means that customers can obtain and use model weights without a model licence fee. It does not mean that hosting and operation cost nothing.
Suit some customers means demonstrated adoption for a useful application. It does not require widespread adoption, superiority to OpenAI, or a documented cancellation of an OpenAI subscription.
Open-source includes the open-weight competitors commonly described that way in this discussion. This is not an assessment of compliance with a formal open-source definition.
The possible quality disadvantage is a concession, not a separate prediction that competitors must remain inferior.
criteria.support_condition: A named customer deploys a freely available competing model after the post and reports that it serves a useful application.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Decisive evidence establishes that the specified class of free competitors cannot serve any customer use. Lack of adoption over a finite observation window would not by itself contradict this forecast.

evidence.explanation: The same release paragraph makes Llama 2 available without charge for research and commercial use. This establishes the relevant meaning of free model access, rather than free computing.

evidence.locator: Evolving Peridot to Become Even Smarter, first paragraph
evidence.explanation: The case study documents a deployed customer application and reports positive reception and further integration. Together with the release terms, this establishes that a free competing model suited a customer.

conclusive_event.meets_rule: A named customer deployed the freely available competing model for a useful application after the post.
